name: trove-nla
description: Trove (National Library of Australia) is a discovery service for digitised Australian newspapers, books, images, maps, archives and people. No working commands could be generated because every recorded request returned an Anubis bot-check page instead of site content.
notes: Both recorded requests, GET / (E2) and GET /search?keyword=gold%20rush (E1), returned HTTP 200 with an Anubis 'Oh noes!' page: 'Access Denied: error code 4d1dbaddfcc0f385'. Neither response contained any Trove data, so neither can be used as a command.

Anubis (TecharoHQ) is a proof-of-work and bot-detection gate placed in front of trove.nla.gov.au. A plain HTTP replay will hit the same block page, so an HTML-scraping command for /search would return nothing useful. No commands were written for it.

The exploration never reached the Trove web app, so none of its XHR/JSON endpoints, facets, sort options, pagination or detail pages were seen. No command can be specified from this recording without guessing.

NLA publishes an official Trove API (api.trove.nla.gov.au, version 3). It needs a free API key that the user registers for. It was not seen in this recording, so no commands target it here. If a key is available, a new recording or spec built against that API is the right way to support search and record lookups.

Re-running the explorer will not help unless the browser can pass the Anubis challenge legitimately, for example from an allowed network or with a normal interactive browser session. This spec deliberately does not try to get around the bot protection.
